rows.evidence: Line 43 is the put-replay winner check. The key is contentType|digest|sizeBytes (:143-145) and sameArtifactRef compares exactly those three fields (contracts/material-access.ts:85-87). The digest is lowercase hex (artifactBodyDigest, contracts/artifact.ts:29-31), so it cannot contain '|' and a contentType containing '|' cannot make two different (contentType,digest,size) tuples collide; both real seams key by artifactBodyKey of the ref they just encoded (body-store.ts:38-39, :71-79; sqlite-body-store.ts:40-46). A winner under the same key with a different ref therefore requires a row stored under a wrong key outside the platform writers; the deleted test supplied exactly such a fabricated row (.dsh-ref/before/tests/data/R3b-body-boundaries.test.ts:44-65, TQ-094).
rows.proposal_note: Keep untested. With the real Map/SQLite seams the guard cannot fire for any platform-written row, but it still turns a wrong-key/foreign row into corrupt instead of returning another body's ref; no tamper test per AGENTS rule 4.

rows.evidence: Line 55 is read's key-consistency check, after rows.get(artifactBodyKey(ref)) (:51). Same argument as A3-029: a row present under that key was written by the platform under the ref it encoded (body-store.ts:38-39; sqlite-body-store.ts:40-46), and key equality implies identical contentType/digest/size (hex digest has no '|'), so the check can only fire for a row stored under a wrong key by an outside UPDATE or a foreign writer (the deleted test used an alien row double: .dsh-ref/before/tests/data/R3b-body-boundaries.test.ts:44-65, TQ-094).
rows.proposal_note: Keep untested, same as A3-029: it is the read-side guarantee that a matching key cannot return a different ref/body without being reported corrupt.

rows.evidence: guarded-revision.ts:20 returns decodeRecordBody's invalid result. decodeGuardedRevision is called only from currentRevisionOf inside a commit transaction (sqlite-record-store.ts:322-331; in-memory-record-store.ts:196-207) with the guard's refKey and the raw stored JSON. Every write path validates the same envelope before writing (record-codec.ts:560-561 for the plan, :730-738 after cursor binding) and upserts under the encoder's refKey (sqlite-record-store.ts:231), so a stored body that fails here means a damaged/hand-edited snapshots row or an old-format row. rows.proposal_note: Keep untested. Deleting the mechanical guard would let a damaged row be waved through as an unchanged revision (the caller maps invalid to corrupt, never to revision_conflict), so keep it; restoring the UPDATE test is forbidden by AGENTS rule 4.

rows.evidence: record-codec.ts:296 rejects a body whose ref canonicalizes to a different key. Read paths pass the stored refKey and stored JSON (sqlite-record-store.ts:352-381; in-memory-record-store.ts:227-252) and the guard path passes the same pair (guarded-revision.ts:19). On the write path the same check runs at :560 (planPreparedCommit) and :730 (after bindPreparedRecords) on encoders that set refKey = canonicalRefKey(snapshot.ref) and json = JSON.stringify(snapshot) (persistence/record-codecs.ts:680-711), so a mismatch needs an outside UPDATE of the row; the two deleted tests did exactly that (.dsh-ref/before/tests/record-store/R3a-transaction-boundaries.test.ts:123, T2-010; .dsh-ref/before/tests/record-store/lookup.test.ts:197, T2-017).
rows.proposal_note: Keep untested. On the write side the check also catches an encoder bug that would file a record under another aggregate's key, and on the read side it is the only place the body ref is compared with ref_key; no tamper test per AGENTS rule 4.
